Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and coping during this postpartum period. 

The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource for us to gauge how you're doing and identify any areas where we can offer additional support. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and within a safe, supportive space. I'm here to listen and help in any way I can.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional state over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. This will give us a clearer picture of how you're doing and what we can do to support you.

Let's get started. I want to begin by asking: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty happy and carefree person, but since having the baby, I just feel so overwhelmed and tired all the time. I do try to watch some funny videos or TV shows, but even those don't seem to make me laugh like they used to. Sometimes, my husband will try to make a joke or be silly, and I'll smile, but it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to bring me joy, and it's hard for me to see the funny side of things when I'm feeling so anxious and worried about the baby's health and safety all the time. I worry about everything - is she eating enough, is she sleeping enough, is she healthy? It's just constant, and it's exhausting. And to make matters worse, I've been having trouble sleeping, which just makes everything feel even more overwhelming. I've been crying a lot more than usual, too - just little things will set me off, and I'll find myself in tears. I feel guilty and inadequate as a mother, like I'm not doing enough for my baby. But despite all of this, I'm trying to stay positive and focus on taking care of myself and my baby. It's just really hard right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I wouldn't say that's been me lately. Like I said, I just feel really overwhelmed and tired all the time. I've been trying to enjoy the little moments with my baby, but it's hard when I'm feeling so anxious and worried about her all the time. And to be honest, I've been feeling really sad and discouraged a lot of the time. It's like, I'll be playing with her or feeding her, and suddenly I'll just start feeling this wave of sadness and worry. It's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not a good enough mom. And that feeling just weighs on me all the time. I've been crying a lot more than usual, and it's just really hard to shake off these feelings of guilt and inadequacy. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, it's just been so hard to muster up any enthusiasm. I mean, I'll think about doing something, like going for a walk or meeting a friend, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed by the thought of getting the baby ready and making sure she's okay... it just feels like too much. And to be honest, even when I do manage to get out and do something, I just don't feel like I'm enjoying it as much as I used to. It's like, I'll be doing something that I used to love, and I'll just feel really flat and unenthusiastic. I've been feeling really disconnected from the things that used to bring me joy, and it's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm going through the motions a lot of the time, and I'm not really feeling any sense of pleasure or enjoyment. It's like, I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think to myself, "I should be happy right now, I should be enjoying this," but I just don't feel it. And that makes me feel even more guilty and inadequate, like I'm not appreciating this time with my baby like I should be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... I do that a lot. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping, I think it's because I didn't establish a good routine. If she's not eating enough, I think it's because I'm not producing enough milk. It's just constant self-doubt and self-blame. I feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm just making mistake after mistake. And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. I'll be trying to do something, like cook dinner or clean the house, and I'll make a mistake, and I'll just feel like I'm a complete failure. I'll think to myself, "I'm just not cut out for this mom thing. I'm not capable of taking care of my baby." It's just really hard to shake off those feelings of guilt and inadequacy. And it's exhausting, because I'm always feeling like I'm walking on eggshells, waiting for the other shoe to drop, waiting for something to go wrong so I can blame myself for it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time. I worry about everything. I worry about the baby's health, I worry about her safety, I worry about whether I'm doing everything right. I worry about things that might happen, things that probably won't happen, but my mind just goes to all these worst-case scenarios. And it's not just about the baby, I worry about my relationship with my husband, I worry about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and the house and everything else. I just feel like I'm always on edge, always waiting for something to go wrong. And sometimes, I'll be sitting there, and I'll just start feeling this overwhelming sense of anxiety, and I won't even know what's causing it. It's just like, my mind is racing, and I feel like I'm going to panic. I've been trying to calm myself down, to tell myself that everything is okay, but it's hard. The worries just feel so real, so plausible. And it's exhausting, because I'm always feeling like I'm on high alert, always waiting for something to go wrong. And even when I'm trying to sleep, my mind is still racing, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, all the things I need to do. It's just really hard to turn it off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, just doing something normal, like feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like, my mind just goes to this worst-case scenario, and I'll start thinking, "What if something happens to the baby? What if I'm not doing enough?" And it's not even like I'm thinking about anything specific, it's just this general feeling of dread and panic. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes, I'll try to take some deep breaths, or I'll try to distract myself by doing something else, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. And it's not just when I'm alone, sometimes it happens when my husband is around, and he'll try to calm me down, but even that doesn't always work. It's just really frustrating, because I feel like I should be able to control my emotions, but sometimes it feels like they're controlling me. And it's hard, because I'm already feeling so tired and overwhelmed, and then these panic feelings come on top of that, and it just feels like too much to handle.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to cook and clean and do all the things that need to be done... it's just feeling really overwhelming. And on top of that, I'm not sleeping well, and I'm feeling really tired all the time, so it's hard to even think straight. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? Like, I'm just going through the motions, but I'm not really in control. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to handle all of this, but it's just feeling like too much. I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. Even simple things, like getting dressed or making breakfast, feel like huge tasks. And the baby's needs are always changing, so I feel like I'm constantly trying to adjust and adapt, but it's hard to keep up. Sometimes I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not doing it right, and that feeling just weighs on me all the time. It's like, I'm just trying to survive each day, but I'm not really living.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and I think it's because I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time. I'll lie in bed at night, and my mind will just start racing, thinking about all the things that are worrying me, all the things that I'm not doing right. And I'll feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and hopelessness, like I'm just not cut out for this mom thing. It's hard to explain, but it's like, I'll be lying there, and I'll just feel this weight on my chest, this feeling of being trapped and unable to escape. And I'll try to calm myself down, to tell myself that everything will be okay, but it's hard to shake off those feelings of unhappiness and anxiety. Sometimes I'll get a few hours of sleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just lie there, staring at the ceiling, feeling miserable. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the fact that I'm not feeling rested even when I do sleep. I'll wake up feeling exhausted, feeling like I've been run over by a truck. And that just makes it harder to deal with the baby, harder to be the mom that I want to be. It's like, I'm just stuck in this vicious cycle of unhappiness and fatigue, and I don't know how to break free.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling any joy or happiness. It's like, I'll be playing with the baby, or feeding her, or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness. I'll think to myself, "I should be happy right now, I should be enjoying this moment," but I just don't feel it. I feel like I'm just pretending to be a good mom, but really I'm just struggling to get by. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, like I'm supposed to be this perfect, happy mom. But the truth is, I'm just not feeling it. I'm feeling overwhelmed, and anxious, and sad. And it's not just the baby, it's everything. I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a shadow of the person I used to be. I miss my old life, I miss my old self. I feel like I'm just stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it. Sometimes I'll cry, just because I'm feeling so overwhelmed and sad. And it's hard, because I don't know how to explain it to my husband, or to my friends and family. I feel like they just think I'm being dramatic, or that I'm just tired. But it's more than that. It's like, I'm just feeling this deep sense of sadness and unhappiness, and I don't know how to make it go away.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be going about my day, and then suddenly I'll just start crying. It doesn't even have to be anything specific that sets me off, just a look, a thought, a feeling... and I'm just overcome with emotion. I've cried in front of my husband, in front of my family, even in front of the baby. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to process it all. Sometimes I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start crying because I'm feeling so exhausted and overwhelmed. Other times, I'll be thinking about something, like how I'm not a good enough mom, or how I'm not doing enough, and I'll just start crying because it's all just feeling so hopeless. It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be strong, like I'm supposed to be able to handle all of this. But the truth is, I'm just not. I'm struggling, and I'm crying, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll try to hold it in, to just push through and pretend like everything is okay. But it's hard to keep it all inside, and eventually it just comes out in tears. I feel like I'm just a mess, like I'm just a big ball of emotions and tears. And it's hard, because I don't know how to make it better, I don't know how to make the sadness and the crying stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

No... I don't think that's something I've considered. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've thought about how I just don't know how to keep going, but I don't think I've ever thought about harming myself. I think I've just felt more like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not a good enough mom, and that's led to a lot of feelings of guilt and inadequacy. But I don't think I've ever considered doing anything to hurt myself. I think I've just felt more like I'm struggling to stay afloat, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. But I do know that I want to be a good mom, and I want to take care of my baby, and I want to be happy and healthy. So, even though things have been really tough, I don't think I've ever considered harming myself. I just feel like I need some help and support to get through this really difficult time.

As a new mother, you're experiencing a range of emotions and challenges that are common during the postpartum period. You've shared feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm, which are affecting your daily life and relationships. It's completely understandable to feel this way, and I'm here to support you. Your feelings are valid, and it's essential to acknowledge the complexity of your emotions during this time.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 26, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Not at all' option</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have not been looking forward to things with enjoyment, stating it's 'hard to muster up any enthusiasm' and feeling 'flat and unenthusiastic' about activities they used to love, which aligns with 'Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>Patient's response indicates frequent and pervasive self-blame, with feelings of guilt, inadequacy, and constant self-doubt, matching 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high level of anxiety and worry, stating they worry 'all the time' and have an 'overwhelming sense of anxiety' that is 'exhausting' and 'hard to turn off', matching the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes experiencing panic for no very good reason 'a few times', which aligns with the 'Yes, sometimes' option, indicating occasional feelings of panic.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>The patient mentions crying a lot lately, feeling overwhelmed and sad, and experiencing hopelessness, which aligns with the option 'Yes, most of the time</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. The symptoms reported, such as persistent <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, <sym>sleep disturbances</sym>, and <sym>feelings of worthlessness and guilt</sym>, align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's emotional distress and difficulty coping with daily responsibilities suggest a need for urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage <med>support group</med> participation for new mothers
3. Recommend <med>therapy</med> or <med>counseling</med> to address <sym>anxiety</sym> and <sym>depression</sym>
4. Develop a <med>self-care plan</med> to improve <sym>sleep hygiene</sym> and reduce <sym>stress</sym>
5. Explore <med>lactation support</med> to address breastfeeding concerns
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
